evidence: Clear package/module structure with well-defined responsibilities (core, parser, directives, plugins, formatters, cli, utils)
Plugins follow a consistent interface (Plugin base class) and are dynamically loaded via PluginsManager
Core components (context, variable, regexp, config) are shared across modules, indicating tight integration
No explicit inter-process communication or service boundaries; all components run in a single process
Parser, formatter, and plugin systems are decoupled but tightly integrated within the same codebase
Directory depth of 4 and 14 packages suggest moderate modularity without distributed service boundaries
Test structure mirrors production structure, indicating monolithic testing approach
risks: Tight coupling between core modules (e.g., variable ↔ context ↔ regexp) may hinder independent evolution
Plugin system is modular but embedded in monolith — scaling or deploying plugins independently is not possible
Shared state via global context (CONTEXTS, get_context/push_context/pop_context) could complicate concurrent execution
